narrative.h2: An anniversary video that doesn't read like a slideshow

sections.heading: Why a couple MV works
sections.body: Most relationship videos are either too long (the full wedding film) or too short (a single Instagram clip). The anniversary or relationship-milestone MV sits exactly in between — 60-90 seconds, scored to the song that was playing on a first date, a road trip, or a wedding dance. It's the format that gets sent privately rather than posted publicly, and it's the one partners actually rewatch on the same date next year.

sections.heading: The shots that always work
sections.body: Relationship videographers come back to the same beats: hands intertwined on a steering wheel, one partner laughing at something off-camera, the back-of-the-head walking-away shot, the matching mug morning, the airport reunion. The cultural canon is built on the anniversary-vlog format pioneered on YouTube, viral proposal videos like Isaac Lamb's Lip Dub Proposal (2012), Hallmark Channel's Christmas romance films, Richard Curtis's Notting Hill and Love Actually as the reference grammar, plus Spike Jonze's warm-orange Her aesthetic shot by Hoyte van Hoytema. Casual phone-quality footage outperforms posed photoshoots - the awkward, unflattering, real moments age well. Tell Tunee which three of those moments mattered most and the MV organizes around them.

sections.heading: Make it the gift
sections.body: The classic use is anniversary morning — a single text with the MV attached, no caption needed. Tunee outputs vertical for sending, widescreen for the eventual living-room screening, and square for the rare time it ends up on a feed, all from one render.
